learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic knowledge on formulation and computer implementation of dynamical system models.
Understand theoretical issues of Laplace and Z transform in their application to describing continuous and discrete linear systems, including systems with distributed parameters.
Develop skills in describing dynamic processes using the state space approach for both linear and non-linear systems.

syllabus_topics: The basic properties of the Laplace transforms
L transform solution of Cauchy problem in differential equations, inverse L transform
Convolution integral transform and transfer function models
Fourier transform, Bode diagram of the linear model
The basic properties of the Z transform
Sampled data linear system, discrete transfer function
Z transform solution of the difference equation, inverse Z transform
Conformal mapping of analytic function, argument increment rule
Discrete approximation of the continuous system by means of L and Z transform
The state space notion, state variables, state trajectory
Introduction methods of state variables, state equations
Steady state of the system, static characteristics, types of singular points
Characteristic function of the linear dynamic system, stability notion
Delay relations in the system model
Methods of numerical solution of the state space equation
Sampling time assessment, stability of the numerical method
Explicit and implicit methods, predictor-corrector
Typical model nonlinearities, saturation
Simulation in Matlab Simulink
Optimization of model parameters, optimality criteria, basic methods of extremum search
